episode.title: Operation Enduring Failure: 25 years after the US invasion of Afghanistan

persons.name: Osama bin Laden
persons.role: Al-Qaeda founder; escaped Afghanistan (Tora Bora or Kandahar) in late 2001 into Pakistan; killed 2011; his files show payments to Abdul Haq al-Turkistani

mentions.quote: Osama bin Laden should not have walked out of Afghanistan
Bin Laden's own personal ledgers, the direct payments of the Lakho Turkestani

persons.name: Hamza bin Laden
persons.role: Son and ideological heir of Osama bin Laden; al-Qaeda released a video indicating he is alive (Sept 2026) seven years after US claimed he was killed; reportedly led Taliban 'red units'; wedding video from Iran safe haven in bin Laden files (2017)
persons.status_detail: US claimed killed c. 2019; Afghan NDS official gave different date/place in Pakistan; al-Qaeda never announced death; new video Sept 2026

mentions.quote: Al-Qaeda is indicating that Hamza bin Laden, one of Osama bin Laden's sons, is alive and well. They released a video of him
We had people telling us that Hamza bin Laden was leading what was known as the Taliban's red units

persons.name: Mullah Omar
persons.role: Taliban founder who sheltered bin Laden, defied US warnings, and escaped the 2001 invasion

mentions.quote: He's the one that sheltered bin Laden and defied America's warning
Mul Omar, you know, stood by his friend and ally Osama bin Laden and he wasn't killed or captured the initial evasion either

persons.name: Ayman al-Zawahiri
persons.role: Late al-Qaeda emir; sided with Jolani over Baghdadi and gave him command of the jihad in Syria; death never confirmed by al-Qaeda

mentions.quote: He had Zawahiri side with him and gave him command of the jihad in Syria
they never confirm Zawahiri's death

persons.name: Saif al-Adel
persons.role: Current al-Qaeda leader based in Iran; admitting it would embarrass the Taliban

mentions.quote: if they have to admit that, say, Balaid, is their leader. And he's based in Iran that does, you know, it's a bad look for them

persons.name: Ahmed al-Sharaa
persons.role: Syrian president; al-Qaeda member since early 2000s, held in US prison in Iraq, took over al-Qaeda's Syrian branch, split from Baghdadi with Zawahiri's backing, swore bayah to Zawahiri; 2016 break approved by Zawahiri's deputy in Syria

mentions.quote: We had him in U.S. prison in Iraq. he was a member of al-Qaeda all the way back in the early 2000s
He had Zawahiri side with him and gave him command of the jihad in Syria, swore an oath of allegiance

persons.name: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi
persons.role: Wanted to control jihad in Iraq and Syria; ejected from al-Qaeda with his cadre, which became the Islamic State

mentions.quote: He had a dispute with Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, who wanted to control the jihad in both Iraq and Syria

persons.name: Abu al-Khayr al-Masri
aliases: Al-Zawa-Hiri's deputy who was in Syria

mentions.quote: his move was approved by him and Al-Zawa-Hiri's deputy who was in Syria at the time

persons.name: Abu Khalil al-Sudani
persons.role: Top al-Qaeda leader killed in a US raid in Paktika (2015); intelligence from the raid revealed the Shorabak camps

events.description: US invasion of Afghanistan (Operation Enduring Freedom) to oust Taliban and kill/capture al-Qaeda leaders
Bin Laden escapes Afghanistan (Tora Bora or Kandahar) into Pakistan due to muddled US decision-making and reliance on dubious Afghan allies
US raid in Paktika kills Abu Khalil al-Sudani; intelligence leads to discovery of Shorabak camps, largest al-Qaeda camp, ~14 years after invasion
CIA releases bin Laden files including Hamza's wedding video from Iran
US (first Trump administration) claims Hamza bin Laden killed in Af-Pak border region; seven years before recording
Al-Qaeda releases video indicating Hamza bin Laden is alive
Washington Post reports 'Al-Qaeda regroups in Afghanistan, 25 years after' citing at least eight training sites in three years; UN says camps in at least 14 provinces
Jolani's break from al-Qaeda, approved by Zawahiri's deputy in Syria
Dispute between Jolani and Baghdadi; Zawahiri sides with Jolani; Baghdadi ejected, forming Islamic State
TTP Times Square plot, which the Obama administration initially called a right-wing plot

key_claims: Operation Enduring Freedom failed its core aims: bin Laden and Mullah Omar escaped in 2001, Pakistan sheltered Taliban leaders, and the Taliban is back in power 25 years later.

Al-Qaeda has training camps in at least 14 of Afghanistan's 34 provinces per the UN; the Washington Post's 'eight training sites in three years' undercounts and 'regroups' ignores continuous presence.
The Shorabak camp (largest in history) was only discovered after the 2015 Paktika raid that killed Abu Khalil al-Sudani.

Al-Qaeda's September 2026 video indicates Hamza bin Laden is alive; the hosts were always skeptical of the US death claim, an NDS official gave a different date/place, and al-Qaeda never announced his death (nor Zawahiri's).
Multiple sources told the hosts Hamza led the Taliban's 'red units' made up of sons of al-Qaeda members married into Afghan families — never published because unverified.
Al-Qaeda avoids confirming Zawahiri's death because admitting Saif al-Adel leads from Iran would embarrass the Taliban.
Sharaa/Jolani was al-Qaeda since the early 2000s, swore bayah to Zawahiri, and his 2016 split was blessed by Zawahiri's deputy in Syria; hosts criticize US embrace of him.
Bin Laden's ledgers show direct payments to TIP leader Abdul Haq al-Turkistani; US death claims about him and Hakimullah Mehsud were wrong before.
